correctness.rationale: The frozen verifier reconstructs the 13-point order from K4 vertices, edges and perfect matchings, computes the order-complex chain complex with 13 vertices, 36 edges, 24 triangles and one-dimensional H_1 over F_2, constructs a non-coboundary cocycle detecting an explicit generator, and exhaustively enumerates isotone self-maps by cover constraints. A fresh independent replay of the same poset and homology detector recovered 562333 isotone self-maps, 24 with nonzero H_1 action, and 24 bijections, with no non-bijective nonzero-action map. Every permutation of the four lower K4 vertices extends uniquely to the six edge and three perfect-matching elements, giving Aut(P) isomorphic to S_4. Order reversal gives the same self-functions for the opposite model.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a complete homological rigidity statement for the cardinality-minimal finite projective-plane model and identifies exactly how direct finite-space maps differ from the much larger classical self-map repertoire. The rigidity and exact automorphism characterization are natural invariants of a canonical minimal model, while the large census supplies reproducibility rather than being the sole value claim.

final_claim: For either of the two opposite 13-point minimal finite models P of the real projective plane, a self-map acts nontrivially on H_1(P;F_2) exactly when it is a homeomorphism; exactly 24 of the 562333 continuous self-maps do so and Aut(P) is isomorphic to S_4.
scientific_limitations: An obscure historical finite-space endomorphism computation could contain the same census under different notation.
The result is specific to the two 13-point minimal models and direct continuous maps; it does not classify maps after refinement or arbitrary finite models.
